'''Asım Orhan Barut''' (June 6, 1926 – December 5, 1994) was a [[Turkish Americans|Turkish-American]] theoretical physicist.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://phys.lsu.edu/~jdowling/barut.html |title=Barut's biography |access-date=2006-06-20 |archive-date=2004-09-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040908075621/http://phys.lsu.edu/~jdowling/barut.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Education ==
He received both his undergraduate diploma and his Ph.D. degree from the [[Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich]] in 1949 and 1952, respectively. He pursued his postdoctoral studies at the [[University of Chicago]] during 1953–1954.

==Academic life==
''Barut'' was an assistant professor at [[Reed College]] during 1954-55 and then joined the faculty at [[Syracuse University]] in 1956. He became a professor of [[physics]] at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder]] in 1962 and served for 32 years.<ref>[http://www.phys.lsu.edu/~jdowling/Barut2.pdf Asım Orhan Barut] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170107034829/http://www.phys.lsu.edu/%7Ejdowling/Barut2.pdf |date=2017-01-07 }} by Marlan O. Scully, ''Foundations of Physics,'' Vol . 28, No. 3, 1998.</ref>

==Research areas==
His research interests centered on [[group theory|group theoretic methods]] in physics.<ref>[http://www.phys.lsu.edu/~jdowling/Barut3.pdf Asım Barut: A Personal Tribute] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170107040229/http://www.phys.lsu.edu/%7Ejdowling/Barut3.pdf |date=2017-01-07 }} by Jonathan P. Dowling, ''Foundations of Physics,'' Vol . 28, No. 3, 1998.</ref> His books include ''Theory of the Scattering Matrix'', ''Electrodynamics and Classical Theory of Fields and Particles'' and ''Representations of Noncompact Groups and Applications''.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Hermann, Robert|title=Review: A. O. Barut, ''Electrodynamics and classical theory of fields and particles''|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1964|volume=70|issue=5|pages=658–660|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183526246|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1964-11148-4|doi-access=free}}</ref> ''Asım Orhan Barut'' was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1966.<ref name="APS"/>
